### [1] [RealVDeblur: One-Step Diffusion for Generalizable Real-World Video Deblurring](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20628)
*Renbiao Jin,Mingxin Yang,Yutian Chen,Junhao Zhuang,Xin Cai,Mulin Yu,Linning Xu,Wenxian Yu,Danping Zou,Shi Guo,Tianfan Xue*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: RealVDeblur uses a diffusion-based, efficient video deblurring pipeline trained with realistic blur synthesis (3D Gaussian Splatting + high-FPS videos) and a frame-wise, distilled one-step generator, plus a Temporal Window Mask for stable long-video inference.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Real-world video blur is highly variable due to camera motion and scene dynamics, and realistic training data is scarce. Robust, efficient deblurring is essential for downstream tasks like mobile imaging and 3D reconstruction.

Method: Data synthesis: physically grounded blur via 3D Gaussian Splatting assets and high-frame-rate videos to cover camera-induced and object-motion blur. Model: a video diffusion prior with frame-wise encoding (no temporal compression in VAE). Inference: distill multi-step diffusion to a one-step generator; introduce a training-free Temporal Window Mask to stabilize long-horizon inference with constant memory.

Result: Empirically, RealVDeblur achieves strong perceptual quality, preserves semantic content, and maintains temporal consistency on unseen real videos, while boosting downstream 3D reconstruction robustness under severe motion blur.

Conclusion: The approach delivers robust, efficient real-world video deblurring by combining realistic blur synthesis with a diffusion-based restoration prior and deployment-friendly inference, enabling stable long-video performance with fixed memory usage.

Abstract: Real-world video deblurring remains challenging due to diverse motion patterns, complex degradations, and the scarcity of realistic training data, yet robust restoration is critical for downstream pipelines such as mobile imaging and 3D reconstruction. This work presents \textbf{RealVDeblur}, an efficient generative framework designed to improve in-the-wild robustness under diverse real capture conditions. First, a large-scale, physically grounded blur synthesis pipeline is constructed from scene-level 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) assets and high-frame-rate videos, providing realistic training data covering both camera-induced and object-motion blur. Second, a video diffusion prior is leveraged for restoration; to better accommodate frame-dependent blur variations, temporal compression in the VAE is disabled and a frame-wise encoding scheme is adopted. For practical deployment on long videos, multi-step diffusion sampling is distilled into an efficient one-step generator, and a training-free Temporal Window Mask stabilizes inference beyond the training horizon with constant memory usage. Extensive experiments on diverse real-world benchmarks demonstrate strong perceptual quality, semantic fidelity, and temporal consistency on unseen videos, as well as improved robustness in downstream 3D reconstruction under severe motion blur. Project page: https://rbjin.github.io/RealVDeblur

</details>


### [2] [Masked Topology Modeling for Self-Supervised Learning on Parametric CAD](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20642)
*Heinrich Jiang,Jennifer Jang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Masked Topology Modeling (MTM) for B-reps: self-supervised pretraining on CAD boundary representations via edge-level topology prediction combined with MoCo-style contrastive learning and region-based reconstruction.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address data scarcity of editable, parametric B-Rep CAD datasets and enable data-efficient pretraining that captures the topology of face adjacencies in B-rep graphs.

Method: 1) MTM masks a fraction of face-adjacency graph edges and trains a head to predict each masked edge's convexity and curve type from post-message-passing face features. 2) Integrates MoCo-style momentum-queue contrastive learning over B-rep-aware augmentations. 3) Adds a BFS-connected face-region masked-reconstruction objective. 4) Pretrains on the ABC dataset and a procedurally generated dataset for downstream evaluation.

Result: The approach yields strong performance across multiple CAD-related benchmarks, demonstrating data-efficient pretraining benefits for B-rep understanding and topology prediction.

Conclusion: MTM, especially when combined with contrastive learning and region-based reconstruction, provides an effective self-supervised pretraining paradigm for B-rep CAD data, mitigating data scarcity and improving downstream tasks involving topology and geometry of faces.

Abstract: Computer aided design (CAD) is ubiquitous: virtually any modern object was designed using editable CAD tools. However, with the shortage of available CAD datasets in its native editable and parametric format, boundary representation (B-Rep), it is ever more important to develop data-efficient methods for this domain.
  We present a new self-supervised pretraining task, Masked Topology Modeling (MTM), that leverages the face-adjacency graph, an induced structure unique to B-reps that the encoder can be asked to reconstruct. MTM masks a fraction of edges and trains a small head to predict each masked edge's convexity and curve type from the encoder's post-message-passing face features.
  We combine MTM with a MoCo-style momentum-queue contrastive learning over B-rep-aware augmentations, a BFS-connected face-region masked-reconstruction objective, and pretraining on the ABC dataset and our new procedurally generated dataset to show strong performance on a number of benchmarks.

</details>


### [3] [Axolotl3D: a Unified Framework for Faithful 3D Shape Completion](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20660)
*Anita Hu,Maria Shugrina*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A unified diffusion-based 3D generation model (Axolotl3D) conditions on images, visibility masks, camera parameters, and partial point clouds to perform occlusion-aware 3D completion, enabling robust multi-view consistency and editing.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current 3D generation methods rely on single-view, complete inputs and lack a unified approach for multi-view, occluded, and multi-modal conditioning; a unified framework is needed for controllable 3D completion under diverse signals.

Method: Axolotl3D jointly conditions a diffusion-based 3D generator on images, visibility masks, camera parameters, and a partial point cloud. The point cloud serves as a geometric anchor; camera parameters enforce multi-view alignment in a shared 3D frame. A unified training strategy synthesizes diverse conditioning regimes from large-scale 3D data to enable cross-modal reasoning and robust completion.

Result: On Toys4K and OmniObject3D, Axolotl3D achieves state-of-the-art performance under both clean and occluded settings, with strong results in real-world reconstruction and geometry-consistent editing.

Conclusion: Axolotl3D provides a unified, multi-modal, occlusion-aware framework for controllable 3D completion, achieving robust cross-modal reasoning and improved multi-view consistency and editing capabilities.

Abstract: Recent 3D generative models produce high-quality geometry from a single image using large-scale priors and diffusion architectures. However, they assume complete visibility and single-view inputs, limiting applicability in multi-view, occluded, or editing scenarios. Although prior works address these challenges individually, they lack a unified framework for controllable 3D completion under diverse conditioning signals. We present Axolotl3D, a multi-modal and occlusion-aware 3D generation model that jointly conditions on images, visibility masks, camera parameters, and a partial point cloud. The point cloud serves as a geometric anchor promoting faithful shape completion, while camera parameters ensure consistent multi-view alignment in a shared 3D coordinate system. A unified training strategy synthesizes diverse conditioning regimes from large-scale 3D data, enabling robust cross-modal reasoning. Experiments on Toys4K and OmniObject3D demonstrate state-of-the-art performance under both clean and occluded settings, as well as strong results in real-world reconstruction and geometry-consistent editing.

</details>


### [4] [ODeform: Learning Continuous 4D Motion for Shape Deformation with Neural ODEs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20670)
*Yordanka Velikova,Mahdi Saleh,Liming Kuang,Benjamin Busam*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ODeform extends Neural ODEs to continuous 4D deformable-object dynamics in 3D by embedding point clouds and material properties into a latent space and solving a continuous-time ODE to model deformation, enabling real-time-like flow without discrete timesteps.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To overcome the limitations of discrete-time deformation methods and computationally heavy physics simulators by providing a continuous-time, data-driven model that supports unseen materials and novel shapes with good generalization and interpolation/extrapolation capabilities.

Method: Encode 3D geometry and physical parameters into a unified latent space; define a neural ODE on latent state representing deformable dynamics; solve ODE over time to obtain continuous deformation flow; evaluate on unseen parameters and real captured objects; provide code and data.

Result: Outperforms baselines in motion prediction under new physical configurations; demonstrates transfer to real objects with novel shapes; enables interpolation and extrapolation in dynamics; approach is computationally efficient and avoids discrete steps.

Conclusion: ODeform provides a scalable, continuous-time framework for deformable-object dynamics, bridging data-driven latent modeling with continuous-time evolution, with demonstrated generalization and potential for real-time applications; code/data will be released.

Abstract: Modeling continuous object deformation is important for many computer vision and robotics tasks, such as manipulation and simulation. Existing approaches rely on learning-based methods or physics simulators to model shape deformations. However, these approaches either use discrete time steps or are too computationally intensive for real-time applications. We present ODeform, a novel extension of Neural Ordinary Differential Equations to continuous 4D dynamics of deformable objects in 3D space. Our method transforms 3D point clouds and physical conditions (like material properties) into a unified latent space. By solving the resulting ordinary differential equations over time, we model deformations as continuous flows within this learned embedding, eliminating the need for discrete time steps while maintaining computational efficiency. We evaluate our approach on unseen physical parameter configurations, showing improved motion prediction accuracy over baseline methods. Our experiments further demonstrate a successful transfer to real 3D captured objects with novel shapes, along with effective interpolation and extrapolation of the learned dynamics. Our code and data will be made publicly available.

</details>


### [5] [Spatially Grounded Concept Bottleneck Models for Trustworthy Breast Ultrasound Diagnosis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20691)
*Moshiur Rahman Tonmoy,Dunren Che,Haitham Y. Adarbah,Afzel Noore*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: SG-CBM grounds concept activations with coarse lesion delineations in breast ultrasound, yielding better diagnostic performance and spatial faithfulness, plus a stress test on supervision quality.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Mitigate unfaithful concept activations and low interpretability in CBMs by leveraging weak anatomical supervision to enforce spatially plausible concept evidence.

Method: Two-zone spatial grounding using lesion mask: in-lesion morphology concepts; posterior acoustic band for posterior phenomena. Train concept maps with grouped spatial grounding; keep semantic fidelity with a linear bottleneck classifier; five-fold stratified group CV; perform Train-corrupt/Test-clean annotation-quality stress test.

Result: Improved diagnostic AUROC and concept macro-AUROC; increased alignment of concept evidence spatially; stress test quantifies impact of supervision quality on diagnosis and faithfulness.

Conclusion: Data-quality-aware supervision design is essential for trustworthy deployable healthcare AI; systematic validation of spatial faithfulness and annotation quality should accompany model evaluation.

Abstract: Concept Bottleneck Models provide interpretable-by-design predictions by mediating diagnosis through human-understandable concepts, but in medical imaging, their trustworthiness is often limited by the quality and granularity of available supervision. In particular, predicted concept activations can be driven by irrelevant regions, leading to spatially unfaithful explanations. We study a data-centric spatially grounded Concept Bottleneck Model (SG-CBM) that leverages coarse lesion delineations as weak supervision to encourage anatomically plausible concept evidence. For breast ultrasound, we derive two clinically motivated zones from each lesion mask: (i) an in-lesion region of interest for morphology-related concepts and (ii) a posterior acoustic band for posterior phenomena. We train concept maps using a grouped spatial grounding objective and preserve semantic faithfulness with a linear bottleneck classifier. Across five-fold stratified group cross-validation, the proposed SG-CBM improves diagnostic AUROC and concept macro-AUROC while markedly increasing spatial alignment of concept evidence. We also perform a Train-corrupt/Test-clean annotation-quality stress test to quantify the impact of supervision quality on diagnosis and spatial faithfulness. Overall, the results underscore the need for data-quality-aware supervision design and systematic trustworthiness validation for deployable healthcare AI systems.

</details>


### [6] [DS@GT ARC at ImageCLEFmed GANs 2026: Geometric Filtering for Privacy-Preserving CT Slice Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20692)
*Eric Regina,Richard Arnaud,Samir Hadi Cisneros*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A privacy-preserving framework for synthetic lung CT slice generation combines Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching with privacy-focused training and a post-generation Supervisor pipeline (autoencoder embeddings, DPP, Stein Kernel Thinning) to filter candidates in geometric latent spaces. It achieves a notable realism-privacy trade-off (Privacy Preservation Score 0.549; FID 0.3290) but persistent re-identification risk remains, indicating deeper patient-specific anatomy is not fully mitigated by preventing direct image copying.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Mitigate privacy risks in synthetic medical imaging while maintaining high visual fidelity, with explicit focus on memorization/membership-inference leakage and the possibility of re-identification from anonymized training data.

Method: Integrates Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching (OT-CFM) with privacy-oriented training; introduces a post-generation Supervisor that filters candidate generations in learned geometric latent spaces using autoencoder embeddings, Determinantal Point Processes (DPP), and Stein Kernel Thinning to reduce memorization and leakage.

Result: Official results show a strong realism-privacy trade-off: best model achieves Privacy Preservation Score 0.549 and an FID of 0.3290. Geometric filtering substantially reduces nearest-neighbor memorization and membership-inference leakage, but persistent patient re-identification scores indicate that preventing direct image copying does not fully remove deeper patient-specific anatomical identity.

Conclusion: The work demonstrates meaningful progress in privacy-preserving medical image generation, highlighting that while geometric filtering improves privacy, a critical frontier remains: preventing deeper patient-specific anatomical identity beyond mere image copying; future work should target stronger protection against re-identification.

Abstract: We present a privacy-preserving framework for synthetic lung CT slice generation developed for the Image-CLEFmed GANs 2026 challenge. The approach combines Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching with privacy-oriented training and a post-generation "Supervisor" pipeline that filters generated candidates in learned geometric latent spaces using autoencoder embeddings, Determinantal Point Processes, and Stein Kernel Thinning. Official results show a strong realism-privacy trade-off, with the best-performing model achieving a Privacy Preservation Score of 0.549 and competitive visual fidelity with an FID of 0.3290. While the proposed geometric filtering substantially reduces nearest-neighbor memorization and membership-inference leakage, persistent patient re-identification scores indicate that preventing direct image copying is not sufficient to remove deeper patient-specific anatomical identity, highlighting an important frontier for future privacy-preserving medical image generation.

</details>


### [7] [U-CFR: Uncertainty-Guided Cascade Forward Refinement for Interactive Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20705)
*Elijah Danquah Darko,Min Xian,Terence Soule,Tiankai Yao,Matthew William Anderson*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: An inference-time framework (U-CFR) for interactive image segmentation that self-corrects via uncertainty-guided pseudo-clicks, using a dual-head network and cascading refinement to improve efficiency and boundary accuracy.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To reduce user effort and accelerate convergence in interactive segmentation by enabling the model to autonomously generate corrective cues without extra supervision.

Method: Propose a boundary-aware uncertainty score that fuses segmentation uncertainty, contour gradients, and explicit edge predictions to place internal pseudo-clicks. Employ a dual-head network with a shared encoder-decoder: a segmentation head for region consistency and an edge head for sharper boundaries. Inference runs a cascade of refinement steps where each stage uses the uncertainty-driven pseudo-clicks to progressively refine the mask.

Result: Experiments show improved click efficiency, better initial mask quality, and improved boundary accuracy; e.g., a reduction of required clicks by over 10% on Berkeley, indicating more intelligent and efficient interactive annotation.

Conclusion: U-CFR demonstrates a principled inference-time self-correction framework that enhances interactive segmentation performance and annotation efficiency by guiding corrective clicks through a boundary-aware uncertainty signal and a dual-head architecture.

Abstract: Interactive image segmentation is critical for efficient image annotation; however, existing methods often require many corrective clicks or rely on passive refinement schemes that converge slowly. We propose Uncertainty-Guided Cascade Forward Refinement (U-CFR), a novel inference-time framework that enables models to autonomously self-correct after each user interaction. U-CFR introduces a boundary-aware uncertainty score that fuses segmentation uncertainty, contour gradients, and explicit edge predictions to guide the placement of internal pseudo-clicks. These self-generated clicks target the most ambiguous boundary regions, providing strong corrective signals without additional manual input. To support this process, we design a dual-head network with a shared encoder-decoder backbone: a segmentation head ensures region consistency, while an edge head sharpens boundary alignment. In inference, U-CFR launches a cascade of refinement steps, where each stage leverages the uncertainty-driven pseudo-clicks to refine the mask progressively. Experiments on standard benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed U-CFR improves click efficiency, initial mask quality, and boundary accuracy. It reduces the required clicks by over 10% on challenging datasets like Berkeley and offers a more intelligent and efficient interactive annotation.

</details>


### [8] [Rethinking Open-World Video Anomaly Detection: Diagnosing Definition Blindness](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20780)
*Inpyo Song,Jangwon Lee*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Open-world video anomaly detection (OWVAD) evaluation often fails to capture definition-conditioned behavior, overemphasizing target-versus-normal separation. The authors diagnose the failure as 'definition blindness', propose definition-conditioned metrics (DC-Disc, DC-DetΔ, DC-SelΔ) and a definition-contrastive rule (DeCoS), and show that many strong baselines lack true definition responsiveness. They demonstrate improvements with DeCoS and advocate evaluating OWVAD via definition-conditioned scoring rather than standard anomaly detection with different prompts.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To ensure OWVAD evaluations reflect a user-defined notion of abnormality, separating definition-specific anomaly scoring from generic anomaly detection, which current metrics conflates.

Method: Decompose dynamic-definition evaluation into target-versus-normal detection and target-versus-other-anomaly discrimination. Propose three definition-conditioned metrics (DC-Disc, DC-DetΔ, DC-SelΔ) to remove shortcuts, and introduce DeCoS, a definition-contrastive scoring rule that subtracts shared anomaly evidence across definitions. Empirically evaluate on UCF-Crime, XD-Violence, MSAD across strong VAD/OWVAD baselines and vision-language models.

Result: Found that target-versus-normal detection dominates (7.2–26.8× weight). Definition-conditioned metrics reveal weak definitionresponse in strong baselines. DeCoS improves the leading baseline by 7.3–16.0 AUROC on DC-Disc and 15.5–28.3 points on DC-DetΔ, indicating better alignment with user-defined anomalies.

Conclusion: OWVAD should be evaluated as definition-conditioned anomaly scoring, not simply as anomaly detection under varying prompts. The proposed metrics and DeCoS provide a more faithful assessment of a model’s ability to follow user-defined definitions of abnormality.

Abstract: Open-world video anomaly detection (OWVAD) is expected to detect events that match a user-specified definition of abnormality. This requirement is stronger than generic anomaly localization: in the same video, changing the definition should change which temporal regions are scored as anomalous. We show that current OWVAD evaluation largely fails to isolate this conditional behavior. Standard VAD metrics and the dynamic-definition protocol can be dominated by target-versus-normal separation, allowing models to obtain strong scores while remaining nearly insensitive to the queried definition. We call this failure mode definition blindness. To explain why it is missed, we decompose dynamic-definition evaluation into target-versus-normal detection and target-versus-other-anomaly discrimination, and find that the former receives 7.2-26.8$\times$ more weight across common VAD benchmarks. Motivated by this diagnosis, we introduce three definition-conditioned evaluation metrics, DC-Disc, DC-Det$Δ$, and DC-Sel$Δ$, which progressively remove normal-frame, generic-anomaly, and multi-event selection shortcuts. Experiments on UCF-Crime, XD-Violence, and MSAD reveal that several strong VAD, OWVAD, and general vision language model baselines localize anomalous moments but exhibit weak definition following, often with near-zero definition-response margins. To validate that the failure is actionable, we further introduce DeCoS, a definition-contrastive scoring rule that subtracts anomaly evidence shared across definitions. DeCoS improves the strongest baseline by 7.3-16.0 AUROC points on DC-Disc and 15.5-28.3 points on DC-Det$Δ$. Overall, our results argue that OWVAD should be evaluated as definition-conditioned anomaly scoring, not as anomaly detection under different prompt labels.

</details>


### [9] [3D-GIMP: When 3D Gaussian Inpainting Meets PatchMatch](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20789)
*Xuening Tian,Dieter Schmalstieg,Shohei Mori*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A hybrid 3D inpainting method that uses a single reference-view generative inpainting plus 3D PatchMatch to propagate textures across views, achieving faster rendering and better view consistency than diffusion-based multi-view inpainting.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To overcome the computational cost and multi-view artifacts (hallucination drift) of diffusion-based 3D scene editing, by enforcing 3D-consistent reconstruction with high-frequency detail.

Method: Compute an appearance prior by inpainting a single key reference view, then propagate textures to other views using a 3D-aware PatchMatch operating on Gaussian Splatting representations, avoiding per-view diffusion.

Result: Achieves competitive inpainting quality with diffusion methods but with faster rendering and improved view consistency; preserves high-frequency details across resolutions and ensures a mathematically consistent 3D reconstruction.

Conclusion: A hybrid 3D inpainting framework that bypasses stochastic diffusion, delivering efficient, coherent 3D object removal in Gaussian Splatting.

Abstract: Recent advances in 3D scene editing have leveraged iterative diffusion models to update input views. However, this process is computationally expensive and struggles to produce sharp details. Meanwhile, ``hallucination drift'' frequently introduces multi-view inconsistencies, leading to structural artifacts when rendering novel viewpoints. To address this problem, we present 3D-GIMP (3D Gaussian Inpainting Meets Patch Matching), a novel hybrid paradigm designed for high-fidelity object removal in 3D Gaussian Splatting. Instead of diffusing every view, 3D-GIMP performs a single generative inpainting on a key reference view, which serves as an appearance prior. We then introduce a 3D-aware PatchMatch algorithm to propagate these reference textures across all remaining views via correspondence matching, effectively bypassing the stochastic nature of frame-by-frame diffusion. By prioritizing reconstructive consistency over iterative generation, 3D-GIMP maintains high-frequency details across arbitrary resolutions while ensuring a mathematically consistent 3D reconstruction. Our experiments demonstrate that 3D-GIMP not only achieves competitive inpainting quality as previous methods using diffusion in multiple views, but also outperforms these methods in rendering speed and view consistency.

</details>


### [10] [Ocular Verification for Virtual Reality](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20790)
*Husanpreet Singh,Robert Tran,Ayushree Kharel,Sudipta Banerjee*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Evaluates ISO/IEC 29794-6 iris quality metrics on VRBiom data; finds some metrics (e.g., margin adequacy) fail for VR; uses generative models to address off-axis gaze, illumination, and reflections; compares unimodal iris and periocular recognition with multimodal score-level fusion; fusion reduces EER by ~11% compared to iris alone; plans to release scripts for reproducibility.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: VR headsets enable seamless interaction but unconstrained iris capture challenges traditional recognition metrics. There is a need to validate and adapt iris quality metrics for VR data and to explore multimodal fusion to improve recognition reliability.

Method: 1) Evaluate ISO/IEC 29794-6 iris quality metrics on VRBiom dataset. 2) Apply generative-model-based techniques to mitigate off-axis gaze, non-uniform illumination, and specular reflections. 3) Perform unimodal iris and periocular recognition and conduct score-level fusion (iris + periocular). 4) Report EER and analyze which metrics fail or succeed; release scripts for reproducibility.

Result: Some metrics, such as margin adequacy, fail on VR-acquired data. Image adjustments primarily benefit periocular recognition. Multimodal fusion lowers EER by approximately 11% relative to unimodal iris recognition performance.

Conclusion: VR-specific iris quality assessment is needed; periocular information helps under VR constraints; multimodal fusion is a viable strategy to improve recognition; reproducibility will be supported via released evaluation scripts.

Abstract: Virtual reality (VR) headsets (e.g., Meta Quest, Apple Vision Pro) provide a seamless user experience due to their fast, frictionless interaction with the physical world in a simulated environment. User authentication relies on biometric cues such as iris in such headsets. However, traditional iris recognition protocols may not be adequate in cases of unconstrained acquisition, which is typical of VR-based data. In this work, we examine three crucial aspects: (1) evaluating ISO/IEC 29794-6 iris quality metrics on VRBiom dataset and analyzing their limitations, (2) addressing data-specific challenges such as off-axis gaze, non-uniform illumination, and specular reflection using generative models, and (3) performing unimodal (iris, periocular) recognition and multimodal score-level fusion (iris + periocular). We observe that some metrics (e.g., margin adequacy) fail on VR-acquired data; whereas, image adjustments primarily benefit periocular recognition, and multimodal fusion lowers EER by ~11% over unimodal iris recognition performance. We will release the evaluation scripts upon acceptance for reproducibility.

</details>


### [11] [SubSplat: High-Resolution Pixel-aligned 3DGS via Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20813)
*Jiun Lee,Jaekwang Kim,Sangmin Lee*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: SubSplat introduces a Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterizer (SPGR) to subdivide primary Gaussians into fine-grained primitives and uses feature aggregation to recover high-frequency details from low-resolution features, enabling high-fidelity and efficient novel-view synthesis with pixel-aligned Gaussian splatting.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: There is a core trade-off in pixel-aligned Gaussian splatting between rendering detail (which benefits from higher input resolution) and computational cost (which grows quadratically with resolution). High-resolution inputs can be expensive, while low-resolution inputs lead to reduced Gaussian density and artifacts.

Method: SubSplat proposes SPGR to subdivide primary Gaussians into finer primitives directly from low-resolution features, enhancing density. It further employs feature aggregation across views to improve reparameterization fidelity and capture high-frequency details.

Result: Experiments on RealEstate10K and ACID show that SubSplat achieves high-fidelity rendering with superior efficiency, validating that the approach alleviates the fidelity-cost trade-off in pixel-aligned Gaussian splatting.

Conclusion: The proposed SubSplat framework effectively resolves the fidelity-versus-cost trade-off inherent in pixel-aligned Gaussian splatting, enabling efficient, high-quality novel-view synthesis.

Abstract: Pixel-aligned Gaussian splatting enables efficient and generalizable novel-view synthesis. However, high-resolution rendering faces a critical trade-off where increasing input resolution improves detail at the expense of quadratically rising network computational cost. Conversely, maintaining low-resolution inputs stabilizes this cost but results in insufficient Gaussian density and artifacts. To address this, we propose SubSplat, which introduces Sub-pixel Gaussian Reparameterizer(SPGR) to subdivide primary Gaussians into fine-grained primitives, restoring structural density directly from low-resolution features. We further enhance the reparameterization quality through feature aggregation, which effectively captures high-frequency details across multiple views. Experiments on RealEstate10K and ACID demonstrate that SubSplat achieves high-fidelity rendering with superior efficiency. Our results validate that the proposed framework successfully resolves the trade-off between reparameterization fidelity and network computational cost inherent in pixel-aligned Gaussian Splatting.

</details>


### [12] [Explainable graph attention network for stress recognition (StressGAT) via differential action units](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20819)
*Thomas Kassiotis,Stefanos Gkikas,Nikolaos Smyrnis,Giorgos Giannakakis*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Graph-based, personalized stress recognition with MIL-driven interpretability.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address limitations of RNN/CNN architectures in capturing non-linear, person-specific facial dynamics for acute stress, and improve clinical interpretability.

Method: Graph Attention Network leveraging relational inductive bias; Differential Action Units to normalize to neutral baselines; MIL attention to localize peak stress intervals; LOSO cross-validation for subject-independence.

Result: Achieves 88.62% accuracy on a 58-participant stress-induction cohort under LOSO; MIL identifies expressivity phenotypes and peak intervals; model offers interpretable, explainable personalized affective monitoring.

Conclusion: Demonstrates a robust, explainable framework for personalized affective monitoring by unifying accuracy and interpretability through graph-based modeling and MIL-driven analysis.

Abstract: Stress is a dynamic process characterized by significant individual variability in facial expression. Traditional architectures, such as Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), often overlook person-specific baselines or lack the representational capacity to model the non-linear temporal progression of distress due to sequential bottlenecks and rigid grid-based constraints. Furthermore, many deep learning models lack the interpretability required for clinical deployment. This study introduces StressGAT, a Graph Attention Network that leverages the relational inductive bias of graph modeling to capture complex facial dynamics that indicate acute stress. By using Differential Action Units, the framework normalizes individual responses relative to neutral baselines to achieve personalized recognition. The proposed model achieves 88.62\% accuracy on a diverse stress-induction cohort (58 participants) using a subject-independent, Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation protocol. Beyond predictive accuracy, the architecture integrates a Multiple Instance Learning (MIL) attention mechanism to identify peak stress intervals and reveal distinct expressivity phenotypes. By simultaneously optimizing for accuracy and interpretability, this framework provides a robust, explainable solution for personalized affective monitoring.

</details>


### [13] [Agentic Designer: Progressive Multi-Agent Collaboration for Structure-Aware Interior Layout Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20866)
*Zhijing Yang,Haocheng Lin,Zhihua Xu,Haojie Li,Keze Wang,Liang Lin,Tianshui Chen*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Multi-agent, structure-aware interior layout generation via Generator-Evaluator-Refiner with Progressive Consensus; paired with InStruct benchmark containing 18k annotated samples; claims superior structural adherence and functional coherence over one-shot diffusion/LLM baselines.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current one-shot generation methods struggle to enforce intermediate geometric constraints, leading to collisions and infeasible arrangements under complex architectural constraints. A structured, verified, iterative design process can improve feasibility and compliance.

Method: Decomposes layout synthesis into proposal, verification, and adjustment stages using three specialized agents: Generator, Evaluator, and Refiner. A Progressive Consensus Mechanism enforces stepwise geometric validation before committing placements. Introduces InStruct dataset (18k parametrically annotated samples) and a suite of structure-centric metrics for standardized evaluation.

Result: Quantitative and qualitative evaluations, plus user studies show substantial improvements in strict structural adherence and design coherence compared with state-of-the-art methods.

Conclusion: Agentic Designer provides a robust, constraint-aware, iterative design process that mitigates error accumulation and delivers more feasible, functionally coherent interior layouts; the InStruct benchmark enables standardized, structure-focused evaluation.

Abstract: Generating realistic interior furniture layouts that strictly adhere to architectural constraints (e.g., walls, doors, and windows) remains a fundamental challenge in automated spatial design. Existing approaches, primarily based on one-shot generation using diffusion models or Large Language Models (LLMs), lack explicit mechanisms for intermediate geometric constraint verification, often resulting in structural collisions and functionally infeasible arrangements under complex room constraints. To address these challenges, we propose Agentic Designer, a progressive, multi-agent framework that formulates structure-aware interior layout generation as an iterative and constraint-verified decision process. By decomposing layout synthesis into modular stages of proposal, verification, and adjustment, the framework coordinates three specialized agents, a Generator, an Evaluator, and a Refiner, through a Progressive Consensus Mechanism. This mechanism enforces stepwise geometric validation and correction before each placement is committed, thereby preventing error accumulation. To facilitate this structure-aware paradigm and standardize evaluation, we establish InStruct, a comprehensive benchmark that integrates a dataset comprising over 18,000 high-quality, parametrically annotated samples with a novel suite of structure-centric metrics. Extensive quantitative evaluations, qualitative analyses, and user studies show that Agentic Designer significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, demonstrating substantial improvements in strict structural adherence and functional design coherence.

</details>


### [14] [ViSTR-Bench: Can MLLMs Reason from Continuous Visual Cues in Dynamic Scenes?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20868)
*Han Li,Si Liu,Zehao Huang,Dongxin Lyu,Longfei Xu,Jiahui Fu,Daxin Tian,Yuliang Xiu,Naiyan Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ViSTR-Bench is a qualitative, four-dimension benchmark for visual spatial-temporal reasoning in MLLMs, featuring 15 subtasks and 1,340 video QA pairs; reveals clear bottlenecks in current models compared to humans.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Addresses the gap where multimodal LLMs excel at static or quantitative tasks but struggle with qualitative reasoning from continuous temporal cues; existing benchmarks emphasize static scenes or exact predictions.

Method: Design-guided evaluation with temporal emphasis, reasoning orientation, and qualitative scoring across four dimensions: Motion Perception, Spatial Relations, Outcome Prediction, and Physical Dynamics; includes 15 subtasks and 1,340 high-quality video QA pairs across tabletop, indoor, and outdoor scenarios; evaluates a broad set of state-of-the-art MLLMs (proprietary, open-source, and specialized models).

Result: Even with strong general video understanding, current models show substantial bottlenecks in complex spatial-temporal reasoning and lag far behind human performance.

Conclusion: ViSTR-Bench provides a comprehensive, qualitative evaluation framework to spur advances in temporal-spatial reasoning in MLLMs. Future work may focus on improving motion understanding, physical intuition, and robust qualitative reasoning under uncertainty, along with expanding scenario coverage and dataset size.

Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have achieved remarkable success across diverse expert-level tasks, but they still struggle with fundamental abilities that humans naturally develop through continuous observation of the real world, such as spatial perception and dynamic reasoning. Recent studies have recognized this gap and introduced dedicated benchmarks to evaluate the spatial-temporal capabilities of MLLMs. However, existing benchmarks mostly focus on static scenes or require exact quantitative predictions, leaving intuitive reasoning from temporal cues largely underexplored. In this paper, we introduce the Visual Spatial-Temporal Reasoning Benchmark (ViSTR-Bench), a novel evaluation suite designed to systematically assess whether MLLMs can perform qualitative reasoning from continuous visual cues in dynamic scenes. Guided by the principles of temporal emphasis, reasoning orientation, and qualitative evaluation, ViSTR-Bench establishes a comprehensive four-dimensional evaluations covering Motion Perception, Spatial Relations, Outcome Prediction, and Physical Dynamics. The benchmark comprises 15 distinct subtasks and 1,340 high-quality video question-answer pairs spanning diverse tabletop, indoor, and outdoor scenarios. Extensive evaluations of a broad spectrum of state-of-the-art proprietary, open-source, and specialized spatial MLLMs reveal that, despite their strong general video understanding capabilities, current models still face substantial bottlenecks in complex spatial-temporal reasoning and remain far below human performance.

</details>


### [15] [Webly Supervised Multi-Label Recognition: Evaluation Benchmark and Dual-Branch Multi-Label Contrastive Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20874)
*Zhihua Xu,Zhijing Yang,Yufeng Yang,Tianshui Chen*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Introduces WS-MLR benchmark (Web-COCO, Web-Pascal) and a Dual-Branch Multi-Label Contrastive Learning (DBMLCL) method to handle noise in webly supervised multi-label recognition, achieving superior results over baselines.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Webly supervised multi-label recognition lags behind single-label work due to lack of unified benchmarks and fair baselines; noisy web data makes learning challenging for accurate multi-label predictions.

Method: Build Web-COCO and Web-Pascal benchmarks with ~300k web images using category-word queries; re-implement baselines under a unified setting; propose DBMLCL with two branches (category-specific instance-level and category-level representations) and use their similarities to identify/correct noisy labels.

Result: DBMLCL achieves superior performance on the WS-MLR benchmark compared to representative baselines, as demonstrated by extensive experiments.

Conclusion: A unified WS-MLR benchmark enables fair comparisons and reveals the effectiveness of dual-branch contrastive learning for mitigating label noise in webly supervised multi-label recognition; the approach advances multi-label learning from noisy web data.

Abstract: Training deep learning models with freely available web images can reduce their dependence on costly manual annotations. Although webly supervised learning has been widely studied for single-label recognition, its multi-label counterpart remains underexplored, partly due to the lack of unified benchmarks and fair comparison protocols. To address this gap, we construct a benchmark for webly supervised multi-label recognition (WS-MLR), including Web-COCO and Web-Pascal, and re-implement representative baselines under a unified setting. The two datasets cover the same 80 and 20 categories as MS-COCO and Pascal VOC, respectively, and contain about 300 thousand images retrieved from the Internet using category-word combinations as search keywords. We further propose a Dual-Branch Multi-Label Contrastive Learning (DBMLCL) framework, which learns category-specific instance-level and category-level representations together with their similarities to identify and correct noisy labels. Extensive experiments on the benchmark demonstrate that DBMLCL achieves superior performance compared to representative baselines.

</details>


### [16] [WhereEdit: Mask-aware Local Latent Editing for One-Step Image Editing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20883)
*Ming Hu,Mingyu Dou,Jianfu Yin,Miaomiao Zhang,Cong Hu,Yao Wang,Bingliang Hu,Quan Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: WhereEdit enables localized adaptive editing for one-step text-to-image generation by region-aware modulation; it improves local edits and preserves structure, validated on PIE-Bench with superior editing quality and maintained efficiency.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current one-step editing relies on global semantic transport and lacks explicit spatial control over the edit region. There is a need to discover editable regions and achieve strong, localized semantic transformation while preserving non-target areas.

Method: Automatic identification of semantically relevant regions from internal model features, followed by adaptive local modulation to enhance target-region edits and maintain non-target regions and structural consistency.

Result: WhereEdit outperforms existing one-step editing methods on the PIE-Bench benchmark in terms of editing quality, while preserving the efficiency of one-step generation. Region-level supervision further demonstrates the importance of explicit spatial reasoning for high-quality one-step editing.

Conclusion: Spatially controlled one-step editing is feasible and beneficial. Localized adaptive editing with region-aware modulation offers a promising direction for high-quality, efficient one-step T2I editing, especially when supported by region-level supervision.

Abstract: Recent one-step text-to-image (T2I) models enable efficient image synthesis and provide new opportunities for real-time image editing. However, existing one-step editing methods primarily rely on text conditioning for semantic transformation, lacking explicit spatial control over \textit{where} to edit. More importantly, even when spatial constraints are introduced, these methods often struggle to achieve strong and stable semantic modifications within the target regions. In this work, we revisit one-step image editing from a spatially controlled perspective and identify two key challenges: discovering editable regions and achieving effective localized semantic transformation. We reveal that existing methods perform global semantic transport, which limits high-intensity local editing under the one-step setting. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{WhereEdit}, a framework that reformulates one-step editing as localized adaptive editing. WhereEdit automatically identifies semantically relevant regions from internal model features and applies adaptive local modulation to enhance target-region editing while preserving non-target areas and structural consistency. Experiments on the PIE-Bench benchmark demonstrate that WhereEdit consistently outperforms existing one-step image editing methods, achieving superior editing quality while maintaining the efficiency of one-step generation. Additional experiments with region-level supervision further highlight the importance of explicit spatial reasoning for high-quality one-step image editing.

</details>


### [17] [Engine-Native Editable 3D World Reconstruction with Objects and Lighting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20889)
*Junhao Chen,Xinghao Chen,Henghaofan Zhang,Zihao Qiao,Saining Zhang,Yongzhi Li,Ruqi Huang,Sisi Li,Yimin Sheng,Jianyi Zhu,Hao Zhao*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A light-aware, engine-native 3D scene parsing benchmark and pipeline (Lumera) that reconstructs object meshes and parametric lights from a single image, achieving strong box detection and near-complete light recall on a large UE5-derived dataset.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To overcome single-image methods' limitations in scene scale, lighting, and engine-native representation, enabling editable, engine-native scenes with explicit light handling.

Method: Lumera-Box and Lumera-Light adapt a Vision-Language Model to predict object boxes and parametric light tuples (x,y,z,r,g,b,I) from a single image, assemble results with per-object mesh reconstruction, HDR environment estimation, and a bounded agentic refinement loop. The Lumera-2K dataset comprises 2,513 UE5 projects, yielding 3.73M components, 63M object instances, 102.6K engine-native parametric lights, and 95.1K camera views; evaluation benchmarks compare against DetAny3D, SpatialLM, N3D-VLM, WildDet3D.

Result: Lumera-Box delivers the strongest overall detection, geometry, semantic, and layout scores in a sanitized box benchmark (merged mAP 0.1141, IoU-B 0.2472, F-score 0.2762); WildDet3D excels in anchor recall. Lumera-Light achieves near-complete non-empty scene recall (0.998) but limited per-light localization (F1 0.209 at 0.5 m); matched lights show median position error 0.261 m, median ΔE2000 4.59, intensity Pearson r 0.628.

Conclusion: Parametric lights are a measurable editable-scene target; results reveal bottlenecks in relation structure, light recall/intensity, and cross-engine generalization, outlining directions to improve engine-native light-aware scene parsing.

Abstract: Editable 3D scene creation requires object instances and lights that can be inspected, moved, and imported into standard engines, yet existing single-image methods largely stop at room-scale geometry, baked/global illumination, or text-driven generation. We introduce Lumera (Light-aware Unified Engine-native Reconstruction and Assembly), a benchmark and reference pipeline for engine-native, light-aware 3D scene parsing from a single image. Lumera-2K is built from 2,513 UE5 projects and provides 3.73M components, 63M object instances, 102.6K engine-native parametric lights, and 95.1K camera views. On this data, Lumera-Box and Lumera-Light adapt VLM to parse object boxes and parametric light tuples (x,y,z,r,g,b,I), which are assembled with per-object mesh reconstruction, HDR environment estimation, and a bounded agentic refinement loop. In a sanitized box benchmark against DetAny3D, SpatialLM, N3D-VLM, and WildDet3D, Lumera-Box obtains the strongest overall detection, geometry, semantic, and layout scores (merged mAP 0.1141, IoU-B 0.2472, F-score 0.2762), while WildDet3D remains stronger on anchor recall. For lights, Lumera-Light recovers almost all non-empty scenes (recall 0.998) but remains limited at individual-light localization (F1 0.209 at 0.5 m); matched lights have median position error 0.261 m, median ΔE2000 4.59, and intensity Pearson r=0.628. These results establish parametric lights as a measurable editable-scene target and expose remaining bottlenecks in relation structure, light recall/intensity, and cross-engine generalization.

</details>


### [18] [MAGE-Vein: Multi-Instance Age and Gender Estimation from Finger Vein Images](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20897)
*Katsuki Tanaka,Koichi Ito,Takafumi Aoki,Masakazu Fujio,Yosuke Kaga,Kanade Oshima,Kenta Takahashi*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Multi-instance, multi-task MAGE-Vein framework for finger-vein age estimation using three-finger feature fusion and gender-conditional optimization to mitigate bias; achieves MAE 6.12 years, r=0.880 on a demographically balanced 402-subject dataset; code release.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Public finger-vein age-estimation datasets exhibit strong demographic biases (e.g., gender) and physiological confounds that limit generalization; a robust method is needed to isolate aging signals from such biases.

Method: A multi-instance, multi-task network (MAGE-Vein) performs hybrid feature-level fusion across three fingers to extract structural aging signs while suppressing local imaging noise. Simultaneously optimizes gender classification to condition the network on gender-related vascular variation, with training conducted on a demographically balanced dataset (402 subjects).

Result: Reported MAE of 6.12 years and Pearson correlation r=0.880 on the balanced dataset; claims to overturn prior consensus about finger-vein limitations and attributes past failures to dataset bias; code provided at GitHub.

Conclusion: The work suggests finger-vein can yield reliable age estimates when demographic bias and gender confounds are mitigated; offers a reproducible framework and dataset considerations that may realign expectations for finger-vein aging studies.

Abstract: Age estimation from finger vein images has been widely considered impractical due to severe demographic biases in public datasets and physiological confounding factors like gender. To overcome these limitations, we propose MAGE-Vein, a novel multi-instance, multi-task learning framework. Our approach extracts robust structural aging signs by employing a hybrid feature-level fusion of three fingers, effectively suppressing local imaging noise. Furthermore, simultaneous optimization of gender classification conditions the network to effectively eliminate gender-specific vascular variations. Evaluated on a demographically balanced dataset of 402 subjects, MAGE-Vein achieves a mean absolute error of 6.12 years and a correlation of 0.880. Our results not only overturn the conventional consensus regarding the limitations of the finger vein modality but also demonstrate that previous estimation failures were primarily artifacts of biased public datasets. Our code is available at https://github.com/gsisaoki/MAGE-Vein.

</details>


### [19] [DINO-VPT: Hierarchical Visual Prompt Tuning for Joint Physical-Digital Face Anti-Spoofing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20900)
*Pierre Gallin-Martel,Mika Feng,Koichi Ito,Takafumi Aoki*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: DINO-VPT is a lightweight, vision-only framework for unified Face Anti-Spoofing that uses hierarchical visual prompt tuning and a Prompt Routing Network to dynamically inject prompts, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy on UniAttackData without multimodal fusion.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Rising diversity of spoofing attacks necessitates unified FAS models capable of detecting both physical and digital threats. VLMs, while generalizable, rely on complex multimodal fusion and external text encoders. A vision-only approach aims to reduce complexity and supervision while maintaining performance.

Method: Hierarchical visual prompt tuning with dynamic prompt injection conditioned on input features via a Prompt Routing Network (PRN). This disentangles diverse spoofing artifacts without multimodal fusion or text encoders, resulting in a lightweight architecture.

Result: On the UniAttackData benchmark, DINO-VPT achieves higher accuracy than state-of-the-art VLM-based methods, demonstrating strong generalization and effectiveness of a vision-only unified FAS model.

Conclusion: A properly structured vision-only architecture with hierarchical prompts and PRN can attain state-of-the-art performance in unified FAS without multimodal supervision, reducing reliance on multimodal fusion and external text encoders.

Abstract: With the increasing diversity of spoofing attacks, there is a growing demand for unified Face Anti-Spoofing (FAS) models capable of detecting both physical and digital threats. While existing Vision-Language Models (VLMs) demonstrate high generalization in this context, they heavily rely on complex multimodal fusion and external text encoders. In this paper, we propose DINO-VPT, a lightweight, vision-only framework leveraging hierarchical visual prompt tuning. By dynamically injecting prompts conditioned on input features via a Prompt Routing Network (PRN), our method effectively disentangles diverse spoofing artifacts without requiring multimodal fusion. Evaluations on the UniAttackData benchmark demonstrate that DINO-VPT achieves higher accuracy than state-of-the-art VLM-based methods. Our results indicate that a properly structured vision-only architecture can achieve state-of-the-art performance in unified FAS without the need for multimodal supervision.

</details>


### [20] [Sidewalk Moments: Are Richer Representations Always More Human-Aligned? Evidence from City-Walk Videos](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20903)
*Liu Liu,Freya Huying Tan,Fábio Duarte*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Richer visual representations do not always yield more human-aligned measures of urban engagement: temporally averaged images (TAIs) can match or outperform full video features in binary engagement tasks, especially in composition-driven scenes, while video features excel in dynamic activity contexts.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Question whether increasing representational richness (from TAIs to full video features) improves alignment with human judgments of urban engagement and whether simpler representations can suffice for perceptual scoring.

Method: Analyze 61 first-person city-walk videos from YouTube, segmented into >50,000 ten-second clips across four modalities: spatiotemporal video features, temporally averaged images (TAIs), audio embeddings, and text-based semantic descriptions. Use Spearman correlation for continuous alignment with human judgments, binary high/low engagement classification across multiple classifiers and quantile thresholds, and an independent MTurk two-alternative forced-choice study. Conduct a gap analysis comparing activity-driven vs composition-driven scenes.

Result: Continous alignment: video features strongest. Binary classification: TAIs match or outperform video across classifiers/thresholds. MTurk: TAIs and full video provide comparable accuracy; text worse; audio near chance. Gap analysis: video advantages in dynamic activity scenes; TAIs better in composition-driven, stable spatial-structure scenes.

Conclusion: Richer representations are not inherently more human-aligned; temporal compression via TAIs can be a principled alternative for perceptual scoring, with implications for dataset design and model selection.

Abstract: We examine whether richer visual representations yield more human-aligned measures of urban engagement, using 61 first-person city-walk videos from YouTube segmented into over 50,000 ten-second clips and represented across four modalities: spatiotemporal video features, temporally averaged images (TAIs), audio embeddings, and text-based semantic descriptions. Spearman correlation analysis reveals the expected ordering along the temporal-richness continuum, with video features showing the strongest continuous alignment. However, this ordering breaks down under binary classification of high- versus low-engagement moments (the paradigm most commonly used to train perceptual scoring models), where TAIs consistently match or outperform video across most classifiers and quantile thresholds. An independent two-alternative forced-choice study on Amazon Mechanical Turk confirms that this parity reflects human judgment: participants identified engaging moments with comparable accuracy from TAIs and full video clips, while text performed substantially worse and audio remained near chance. Gap analysis reveals a functional dissociation: video features are advantaged in activity-driven scenes with dynamic content, whereas TAIs better align with human judgments in composition-driven scenes dominated by stable spatial structure. These findings challenge the assumption that richer representations are inherently more human-aligned, and suggest that perceptually grounded temporal compression can be a principled alternative to full video encoding.

</details>


### [21] [FA-LAM: Focus-Aware Large Avatar Model for One-Shot 4D Animatable Gaussian Head](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20922)
*Yingdong Hu,Yisheng He,Yiming Jiang,Zehong Lin,Steven Hoi,Jun Zhang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: FA-LAM is a focus-aware avatar model for one-shot animatable Gaussian head creation with static 3D and dynamic 4D reconstruction. It mitigates two key limitations of prior SOTA methods—noisy attention activations and conflicts between reconstruction and animation—via symmetric semantic attention regularization, a dual-phase training pipeline, and memory-efficient multi-view 4D autoregressive token fusion, delivering superior quality at large view angles and in fine facial regions.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Prior state-of-the-art approaches for full-head reconstruction and animation suffer from incorrect/noisy attention activations and conflicting tasks between reconstructing a high-fidelity head and animating it. This hampers 3D full-head quality, especially for large viewing angles. A focus-aware design and task disentanglement are needed to enable robust one-shot head creation and scalable 4D reconstruction.

Method: Introduce symmetric and semantic attention regularization leveraging the structural symmetry of human heads. Develop a dual-phase training pipeline that decouples large-view head hallucination from animation capabilities. Implement an autoregressive core with visibility-aware token fusion to enable memory-efficient multi-view and streaming 4D reconstruction.

Result: FA-LAM achieves higher-quality animatable Gaussian full-head reconstructions, with notable improvements in fine facial regions and large viewing angles. The method supports static 3D and dynamic 4D reconstruction in a memory-efficient manner, outperforming prior approaches.

Conclusion: By addressing attention semantics and task disentanglement, FA-LAM provides a robust, scalable solution for one-shot animatable head reconstruction and animation, enabling high-fidelity 3D/4D results and efficient multi-view streaming.

Abstract: We propose FA-LAM, a Focus-Aware Large Avatar Model for one-shot animatable Gaussian head creation, while simultaneously enabling static 3D and dynamic 4D full-head recovery. The core of our method lies in a thorough analysis of the attention mechanisms and the entangled reconstruction and animation training pipeline adopted by prior state-of-the-art approaches. Our analysis identifies two main factors that compromise the quality of 3D full-head generation: (1) incorrect and noisy attention activations, and (2) conflicts between the tasks of reconstruction and animation. To address the first issue, we introduce a symmetric and semantic attention regularization strategy that leverages the inherent semantics and structural symmetry of human heads. To disentangle the objectives of reconstruction and animation, we develop a novel dual-phase training pipeline that separates the model's capabilities for large-view hallucination and animation into distinct modules. Moreover, we enhance our model to support multi-view and streaming 4D reconstruction in an efficient and memory-friendly manner through a core autoregressive modification with tailored visibility-aware token fusion. Collectively, these innovations enable FA-LAM to reconstruct animatable Gaussian full heads with superior quality, particularly in fine facial regions and large viewing angles.

</details>


### [22] [MagicMakeup: A Region-Controllable Diffusion Transformer for High-Fidelity Makeup-Transfer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20924)
*Ziyi Wang,Siming Zheng,Yang Yang,Shusong Xu,Hao Zhang,Bo Li,Changqing Zou,Peng-Tao Jiang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: A diffusion-transformer makeup transfer method with region-level control and robustness, using Token-Aligned Region Gating and Cross-Modal Perception Guidance, plus a 1024x1024 synthetic/real benchmark; shows improved regional control, fidelity, and identity preservation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address key challenges in region-controllable makeup transfer: pixel-to-attention misalignment causing spillover, coupling between makeup attributes and identity under two-image conditioning, and lack of high-resolution, identity-consistent, region-labeled data for fine-grained supervision.

Method: MagicMakeup is a diffusion-transformer framework with spatial constraints and concept disentanglement. It introduces Token-Aligned Region Gating to align pixel masks with attention for region-specific logit gating, and Cross-Modal Perception Guidance to align text and image features for clearer transfer/preservation concepts. It also provides a pipeline to generate 1024×1024 data pairs via region-specific makeup removal and a unified benchmark in synthetic and real settings.

Result: Extensive quantitative and qualitative evaluations show improved regional controllability, makeup fidelity, and identity preservation, with robustness across styles, races, and poses.

Conclusion: MagicMakeup enables high-fidelity, region-controllable makeup transfer with strong identity preservation and introduces data/benchmarking pipelines to support fine-grained supervision and evaluation.

Abstract: Makeup-transfer applies the reference makeup to the source face while preserving the source identity. Despite advances in full-face editing by diffusion-based methods, strong regional controllability, makeup fidelity, and identity preservation remain challenging. The reasons are (i) pixel-to-attention misalignment that causes spillover into non-target areas and weakens regional control; (ii) unclear transfer/preservation concept separation under two-image conditioning, leading to coupling between makeup attributes and identity; and (iii) the lack of a high-resolution dataset that is identity-consistent and region-labeled for fine-grained supervision. In this paper, we propose MagicMakeup, a diffusion transformer-based framework for region-controllable and high-fidelity makeup transfer, built on spatial constraints and concept disentanglement. To enable precise region-specific editing while preserving identity, we propose Token-Aligned Region Gating, which aligns pixel masks with attention and applies region-specific logit gating. To clarify the concepts of transfer and preservation, we further introduce Cross-Modal Perception Guidance, which aligns text and image features to enhance cross-modal concept perception. We also design a pipeline for the generation of 1024 x 1024 data pairs through region-specific makeup removal and establish a unified benchmark in synthetic and real settings. Extensive quantitative and qualitative experiments show that MagicMakeup improves regional controllability, makeup fidelity, and identity preservation, with strong robustness across styles, races, and poses.

</details>


### [23] [Ms. Forcing: Efficient Streaming Video Generation with Multi-Scale Patchification and Attention](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20940)
*Zekun Li,Xiaoyan Cong,Hongyu Li,Zhiyang Dou,Chuan Guo,Abhay Mittal,Sizhe An,Srinath Sridhar*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Ms.Forcing is a streaming video diffusion method that adapts spatial granularity to per-state noise using MSP and MSSA, with H-DMD to align training and inference. It yields real-time performance (22.84 FPS on H200) and faster throughput than Rolling Forcing, with improved VBench scores for short and long videos.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Streaming video diffusion models face high latency due to nested autoregressive and denoising loops. Rolling-window approaches reduce some cost but still apply uniform high spatial granularity. The work aims to reduce redundancy and compute by adapting granularity to noise levels while maintaining a static computation graph.

Method: Multi-Scale Patchification (MSP): assign coarser patches to noisier states to reduce active-token count; Multi-Scale Self-Attention (MSSA): adjust attention density to match each query scale; fixed window scheduling to keep a hardware-friendly static graph; Homogeneous-Noise-Level DMD (H-DMD): assemble each fake video from clean predictions sharing the same source noise level to reduce training-inference mismatch; training benefits from multi-scale design offsetting overlapping window backpropagation costs.

Result: Empirical results show Ms.Forcing reaches 22.84 FPS on a single H200 GPU, 39.6% faster than Rolling Forcing, and significantly improves VBench scores in both short- and long-video generation scenarios, validated by quantitative and qualitative experiments.

Conclusion: The proposed multi-scale framework reduces computational cost and token/attention load in streaming video diffusion while preserving or improving generation quality. The fixed scheduling yields a hardware-friendly graph, and H-DMD mitigates training-inference mismatch. Overall, Ms.Forcing enables real-time streaming video generation with improved throughput and fidelity.

Abstract: Streaming video diffusion models have made substantial progress toward interactive and dynamic world simulation, but the nested autoregressive and denoising loops of conventional next-frame generation hinder real-time deployment. Recent rolling-window methods pipeline denoising across multiple consecutive frames at different noise levels, improving throughput and long-horizon stability. However, they tokenize every state at the same fine spatial granularity, leaving substantial noise-dependent redundancy in the joint denoising window. We propose Ms.Forcing, an efficient streaming video generation paradigm that adapts spatial granularity to each state's noise level. Its Multi-Scale Patchification (MSP) assigns coarser patches to noisier states, reducing the active-window token count by 45%, while Multi-Scale Self-Attention (MSSA) matches the density of visible non-sink keys and values to each query scale to further reduce attention cost. Because both schedules are fixed by window position, Ms.Forcing retains a static, hardware-friendly computation graph. We further introduce Homogeneous-Noise-Level DMD (H-DMD), which assembles each fake video from clean predictions sharing the same source noise level, thereby reducing the mismatch between DMD training sequences and inference-time rollouts. The multi-scale design helps offset the additional training cost of backpropagating through overlapping windows. We include both quantitative and qualitative experiments to show that Ms.Forcing reaches 22.84 FPS on a single H200 GPU, 39.6% faster than Rolling Forcing, while significantly improving VBench scores in both short video and long video generation setting.

</details>


### [24] [RECO: Region-Aware Compensation for Extrinsic Perturbations in Roadside 3D Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20947)
*Junsheng Du,Zhaocheng He,Yuhuan Lu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: RECO is a region-aware extrinsic compensation framework for roadside 3D object detection that mitigates camera extrinsics perturbations via piecewise 6-DoF pose offsets, near/far region partition with a sigmoid blend, and an auxiliary reprojection loss, yielding robustness to yaw and vertical miscalibration on DAIR-V2X-I and Rope3D.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Camera extrinsics are highly sensitive in BEV-based roadside 3D detection; small extrinsic errors are amplified by projective geometry, causing feature misalignment and localization degradation.

Method: Predicts a learnable boundary to split the scene into near/far regions; estimates region-specific 6-DoF pose corrections; uses a differentiable sigmoid gate to blend compensated geometries; employs an auxiliary reprojection loss matching 2D projected GT boxes to 2D annotations, optimized with standard detection loss.

Result: Demonstrates consistent improvements over SOTA baselines under yaw and z-axis perturbations on DAIR-V2X-I and Rope3D benchmarks; generalizes from transient perturbations to persistent miscalibration; retains strong performance under calibration uncertainty.

Conclusion: RECO effectively mitigates extrinsic perturbations in roadside 3D detection by region-aware correction and smooth fusion, improving robustness and stability of BEV sampling and optimization, with strong cross-dataset validation.

Abstract: In intelligent transportation systems, roadside 3D object detection provides wide-area perception crucial for traffic understanding, cooperative early warning, and safe autonomous driving. However, existing methods suffer from high sensitivity to camera extrinsics; even slight deviations (whether manifesting as transient jitter or persistent drift) can be significantly amplified by projective geometry. This cascade results in severe feature misalignment and degraded localization. To mitigate this limitation, we propose RECO, a region-aware extrinsic compensation framework that corrects extrinsics using piecewise 6-DoF pose offsets. RECO predicts a learnable range boundary to partition the scene into near and far regions, estimating region-specific pose corrections. A differentiable sigmoid gate then smoothly blends the two compensated geometries to preserve continuous BEV sampling and facilitate stable optimization. To supervise the refinement of extrinsics, we introduce an auxiliary reprojection loss that compares 2D bounding boxes projected from 3D ground truth against 2D annotations, optimizing it jointly with the standard detection objective. Extensive experiments on the DAIR-V2X-I and Rope3D benchmarks under extrinsic perturbations demonstrate consistent improvements over state-of-the-art baselines across both yaw and $z$-axis deviations. RECO also generalizes from transient perturbations to persistent shifts, maintaining highly competitive performance under strict calibration uncertainty.

</details>


### [25] [FSB-Net: Frequency-Spatial Boundary Network for Brain Stroke Lesion Segmentation in Non-Contrast CT](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20955)
*Linke Fan,Xianglong Li,Huixin Huang,Kai Shu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: FSB-Net introduces a frequency-spatial boundary-aware framework for NCCT brain stroke lesion segmentation, using Wavelet Boundary Detection, Frequency-Spatial Cross-Attention, and Spectral Boundary Loss on a PVTv2-B2 encoder to achieve state-of-the-art Dice, IoU, and HD95 on a public Brain Stroke CT dataset.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: NCCT stroke lesion segmentation suffers from low tissue contrast and heterogeneous lesion morphology, with uncertain boundaries due to partial volume effects. Explicit boundary modeling is lacking in existing region-focused DL methods, hindering accurate delineation and downstream volumetry.

Method: Three components: (i) Wavelet Boundary Detection Head (WBDH) applying discrete wavelet transform to multi-scale encoder features to extract high-frequency boundary representations; (ii) Frequency-Spatial Cross-Attention Module (FSCAM) enabling bidirectional attention between wavelet boundary features and spatial decoder features to boost boundary cues; (iii) Spectral Boundary Loss penalizing high-frequency discrepancies in Fourier domain to sharpen boundaries. Uses a PVTv2-B2 encoder; evaluated on a public Brain Stroke CT dataset including ischemic and hemorrhagic cases.

Result: FSB-Net outperforms U-Net, UNet++, MANet, and DeepLabV3+ across all metrics, achieving state-of-the-art mean Dice, mean IoU, and HD95 on the Brain Stroke CT dataset for both ischemic and hemorrhagic subtypes.

Conclusion: Frequency-spatial boundary modeling via wavelets and spectral loss yields sharper, more accurate lesion boundaries and improved segmentation performance on NCCT stroke imaging; suggests potential for better volumetric assessment and treatment planning; future work could expand validation to more datasets and modalities, and optimize computational efficiency.

Abstract: Accurate segmentation of brain stroke lesions in non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT) scans is critical for rapid clinical decision-making, yet remains difficult due to the low contrast between lesion and normal brain tissue, heterogeneous lesion morphology across ischemic and hemorrhagic subtypes, and ambiguous boundaries caused by partial volume effects. Current deep learning approaches primarily optimize region-level overlap but lack explicit boundary modeling, leading to imprecise delineation that can affect volumetric assessment and treatment planning. We propose FSB-Net, a frequency-spatial boundary network that leverages frequency-domain analysis for boundary-aware stroke lesion segmentation. FSB-Net introduces three components: (i) a Wavelet Boundary Detection Head (WBDH) that applies the discrete wavelet transform to multi-scale encoder features, extracting high-frequency sub-bands as boundary representations; (ii) a Frequency-Spatial Cross-Attention Module (FSCAM) that performs bidirectional attention between wavelet boundary features and spatial decoder features for selective boundary enhancement; and (iii) a Spectral Boundary Loss that penalizes high-frequency discrepancies in the Fourier domain to optimize boundary sharpness. Built on a PVTv2-B2 encoder, FSB-Net is evaluated on a public Brain Stroke CT dataset containing both ischemic and hemorrhagic cases. Experimental results show that FSB-Net outperforms U-Net, UNet++, MANet, and DeepLabV3+ across all metrics, achieving state-of-the-art performance in mean Dice, mean IoU, and HD95.

</details>


### [26] [Unsupervised Metal Artifact Reduction in Dental CBCT using Fine-tuned Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20977)
*G. L. T. Chamika,S. N. A. Dhanapala,P. H. S. V. Nimalaweera,Maheshi B. Dissanayake,Ruwan D. Jayasinghe*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Unsupervised CycleGAN-based MAR for dental CBCT using unpaired ToothFairy data; U-Net generators and PatchGAN discriminators; real-time inference; clinician-in-the-loop recommended.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address metal artifacts in dental CBCT without requiring unattainable voxel-aligned paired datasets by leveraging unpaired training data to achieve high-fidelity restoration while preserving anatomical morphology.

Method: Unpaired CycleGAN framework with U-Net generators and PatchGAN discriminators trained on ~4,000 images from the ToothFairy dataset; designed to minimize generative hallucinations and preserve morphology; achieves 3.03 ms per-slice inference.

Result: BRISQUE improved by 34.6%; FID reduced from 207.03 to 157.04; SSIM of 0.9105; real-time inference; expert validation confirms high fidelity; recommended as clinical decision-support with human-in-the-loop oversight.

Conclusion: Presents a scalable, high-fidelity MAR solution for dental implant CBCT imaging, reducing artifacts while preserving anatomical detail; suitability for clinical deployment as a decision-support tool with safeguards.

Abstract: Metal artifacts generated by dental implants significantly degrade cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) volumes, obscuring critical anatomical structures and compromising diagnostic precision. To address this, an unsupervised deep learning framework has been proposed for Metal Artifact Reduction (MAR) utilizing a Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Network (CycleGAN) optimized for high-fidelity restoration. Unlike supervised methods that rely on unattainable voxel-aligned paired datasets, the proposed approach leverages an unpaired dataset of approximately 4,000 images, curated from the public ToothFairy dataset. The architecture integrates U-Net-based generators and PatchGAN discriminators, specifically tuned to mitigate generative hallucinations and preserve morphological integrity. Quantitative benchmarking on a held-out test set demonstrates a 34.6\% improvement in the Blind/Referenceless Image Spatial Quality Evaluator (BRISQUE) score, a substantial reduction in Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) from 207.03 to 157.04, and a superior Structural Similarity Index Measure (SSIM) of 0.9105. The framework achieves real-time efficiency with a 3.03 ms inference time per slice, effectively suppressing artifacts while preserving anatomical detail.
